mainTopic: The meaning of each part of the public fast-day ceremony, the elder's call to real תשובה, and who should lead the prayers
overview: The גמרא explains the public fast-day ceremony for rain. It finishes saying why others put ashes on the leaders. רבי יצחק says the ashes go where the תפילין are worn. Next it gives a memory list (סימן) and explains each practice. The people go out to the town square, either to humble themselves in public or to make a kind of exile that atones. The תיבה is brought out to show that our sins exposed a hidden, holy object. The people wear sackcloth, ashes go on the תיבה and on every head, and the people go to the cemetery, with two reasons and a practical difference given for each. Along the way, רבי לוי בר חמא and רבי חנינא also explain the name הר המוריה. The גמרא then explains who gives the words of rebuke: an elder who is also a חכם. Those words teach that תשובה and good deeds, not sackcloth and fasting, bring atonement, as seen with אנשי נינוה and in רב אדא בר אהבה's parable of the שרץ. Finally, a ברייתא describes the ideal שליח ציבור for the fast day, and the Sages see these qualities in רב יצחק בר אמי.

steps.title: End of the reason others place the ashes on the leaders
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the earlier teaching: being shamed by others is a greater humbling than shaming yourself.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...is not like someone who is shamed by others.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the tail end of a teaching that started before this section. It explains why someone else, and not the leader himself, puts the ashes on the head of the נשיא and the אב בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Humbling yourself is one thing, but being humbled by someone else is much stronger. So on the fast day, others put the ashes on the leaders to make their humbling as strong as possible.

phrases.english: to one who is shamed by others.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמִתְבַּיֵּישׁ מֵאֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Others place the ashes on the leaders, because being shamed by others is a greater humbling.

steps.title: Where on the head are the ashes placed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks exactly where the ashes are put on the leaders' heads.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where do they put them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple practical question: on what part of the head do the ashes go? This sets up רבי יצחק's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said ashes go on the heads of the leaders but did not say where exactly. The גמרא wants the precise spot.

phrases.english: And where does one place them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means the ashes put on the leaders' heads.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכָא מַנַּח לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of placing ashes, now asking for the exact spot.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact place on the head where the ashes are put.

steps.title: The ashes go where the תפילין are worn
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says the ashes are placed where the תפילין go, and brings a פסוק from ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: On the place of the תפילין, as it says: "To appoint for the mourners of ציון, to give them an ornament instead of ashes."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question: the ashes go on the spot of the head תפילין. He supports this with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links "ornament" (פאר) with "ashes" (אפר), showing they sit in the same place. The גמרא reads פאר as the תפילין, so the ashes go where the תפילין go.

keyTerms.meaning: on the place of the תפילין
ornament; here understood as the תפילין

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
On the place of the tefillin.
As it is said: "To appoint for the mourners of Zion,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 61:3

phrases.english: to give them an ornament instead of ashes."
phrases.notes: The "ornament" here is the תפילין, so the ashes sit in that same spot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: בִּמְקוֹם תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of where the ashes go.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On the place of the head תפילין, based on ישעיהו 61:3.
steps.whatToRemember: On the fast day, others put ashes on the leaders' heads, right where the תפילין are worn.

steps.title: A memory list for the coming teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a list of key words to help remember the order of the teachings that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Square, ark, and sackcloth, ashes, ashes, burial, and מוריה: this is a memory list.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא lists key words, one for each teaching coming up, so we can remember their order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word stands for one upcoming question: why go to the square, why bring out the ark, why wear sackcloth, and so on. It teaches no law itself; it is a map of what comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: a memory aid, a list of key words
the ark that holds the ספר תורה

steps.confusionAlert: This list is not a ruling. It just helps you remember the order of the teachings that follow.

phrases.english: Square, ark, and sackcloth,
ashes, ashes, burial,
and Moriah: a memory aid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רְחוֹב, תֵּיבָה, וְשַׂקִּים, אֵפֶר, אֵפֶר, קְבוּרָה, וּמוֹרִיָּה סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section explaining the reasons behind each part of the fast-day ceremony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory list for the series of explanations that follow.

steps.title: Why do they go out to the town square?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the community goes out to the square on the fast day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do they go out to the square?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the first item on the list: why the prayers are moved out to the town square. This sets up two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the people pray in the square, not in the בית כנסת. The גמרא wants to know what this is meant to show.

keyTerms.meaning: they go out to the square

phrases.english: Why do they go out to the square?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה יוֹצְאִין לָרְחוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the first item from the memory list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning behind going out to the town square.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבא: We humble ourselves in public
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא says going out shows that private prayer was not answered, so now we humble ourselves in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: It is as if to say, we cried out in private and were not answered, so we will shame ourselves in public.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא gives the first reason for going out to the square. It is a public act of humbling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praying inside the בית כנסת is private. When that did not work, the people step up their humbling by doing it openly. For him, the key is that it is public.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said:
To say: We cried out in private
phrases.notes: "In private" means inside the בית כנסת.

phrases.english: and we were not answered;
we will shame ourselves in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to why they go to the square.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a public humbling after private prayer was not answered.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Going out is a kind of exile that atones
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says leaving for the square is like going into exile, and the exile brings atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: We have gone into exile; may our exile atone for us.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different reason for going out to the square. Leaving our usual place is like going into exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, the point is not the public shame. It is the leaving of our normal place of prayer, which is like a small exile that brings atonement.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
We have gone into exile; may our exile atone for us.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: גָּלִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different reason for the same practice.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Leaving for the square is a form of exile, and exile atones.

steps.title: What difference is there between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the two explanations ever lead to a different practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks if there is a real, practical difference between רבי חייא בר אבא and ריש לקיש. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons agree that we go to the square. The גמרא wants a case where one reason would allow something and the other would not.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is between them?
phrases.notes: He means: is there any case where these two reasons give a different result?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where the two reasons differ.

steps.title: Moving from one בית כנסת to another
steps.stepSummary: The difference is when they move from one בית כנסת to another instead of going to the square.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when they moved from one בית כנסת to another בית כנסת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the case where the two reasons split: moving from one בית כנסת to a different one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, this move still counts as exile, so it is enough. For רבי חייא בר אבא, the prayer is still indoors and private, so it is not the public humbling he requires.

keyTerms.meaning: there is a difference between them
where they went into exile, moved

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא בר אבא: going out is about public humbling. ריש לקיש: going out is about exile. Moving between two בתי כנסיות counts only for ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where they went out from one synagogue
to another synagogue.
phrases.notes: This counts as "exile" for ריש לקיש, but it is still private for רבי חייא בר אבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ, דְּגָלוּ מִבֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא לְבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the difference between the two reasons.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two reasons differ when they move from one בית כנסת to another: it counts as exile, but it is not public.

steps.title: Why do they bring the ark out to the square?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next item on the list and asks why the תיבה is brought out to the square.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they bring the ark out to the town square?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the second item on the memory list: why the ark is taken out of the בית כנסת. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking out the people is one thing, but the ark is a holy object normally kept inside. The גמרא wants to know the point of exposing it.

phrases.english: And why do they bring out the ark
to the square of the town?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמָּה מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הַתֵּיבָה לִרְחוֹבָהּ שֶׁל עִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item (תיבה) from the memory list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning behind bringing the ark out to the square.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: Our holy, hidden object was exposed because of our sins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says bringing out the ark shows that our sins caused a modest, hidden object to be exposed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: It is as if to say, we had a modest, hidden object, and it was disgraced because of our sins.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains the meaning of bringing out the ark. It is a sign of shame caused by our sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ark is normally kept hidden and honored inside. Putting it out in the open shows the people that their sins brought this lowering, which moves them to do תשובה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, לוֹמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: To say:
We had a modest vessel,
phrases.notes: The "modest vessel" is the ark, which is normally kept inside.

phrases.english: and it has been disgraced because of our sins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, לוֹמַר: כְּלִי צָנוּעַ הָיָה לָנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the ark is brought out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It shows that our sins caused a holy, hidden object to be put on display.
steps.whatToRemember: The ark is brought out to the square to show that our sins exposed a holy, hidden object.

steps.title: Why do they wear sackcloth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next fast-day practice and asks why people cover themselves in sackcloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they cover themselves in sackcloth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on the fast-day list and asks for its reason. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Same pattern as the question about the תיבה in Step 10. The גמרא wants to know what message wearing שק sends.

keyTerms.meaning: sackcloth, a rough cloth like animal hair

phrases.english: And why do they cover themselves in sackcloth?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמָּה מִתְכַּסִּין בְּשַׂקִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next practice after the תיבה was explained in Step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for wearing sackcloth on a fast day

steps.title: Sackcloth shows we are like animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא says sackcloth expresses that we feel as low as animals before הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: It is to say, 'We are considered like an animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers that the sackcloth is a statement of humility. We admit we are like animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sackcloth is rough, like an animal's hide. Wearing it makes the point that, because of our sins, we see ourselves as no better than animals.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said:
To say: Behold, we are considered like an animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sackcloth expresses that we are considered like animals

steps.title: Why put burnt ashes on the ark?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why burnt ashes are placed on top of the תיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they put burnt ashes on top of the ark?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the next practice, the ashes put on the תיבה. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 explained why the תיבה is taken out to the square. Now the גמרא asks a separate question: why ashes are put on it.

keyTerms.meaning: the ark holding the ספרי תורה

phrases.english: And why do they place burnt ashes
on top of the ark?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמָּה נוֹתְנִין אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה עַל גַּבֵּי תֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next practice on the list
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for putting ashes on the תיבה

steps.title: God is with us in our trouble
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן פזי says the ashes on the תיבה show that הקב״ה is with us in our trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן פזי said: It is as if to say, 'I am with him in trouble.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן פזי explains the ashes with a פסוק that says הקב״ה is with Israel when they suffer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תיבה stands for הקב״ה's presence. Putting mourning ashes on it shows that He, so to speak, shares our pain.

keyTerms.meaning: I am with him in trouble

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Pazi said:
As if to say: "I am with him in trouble."
phrases.notes: תהלים 91:15

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ashes show הקב״ה is with Israel in their trouble

steps.title: A different verse with the same idea
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives another פסוק for the same idea: in all their trouble, He is troubled.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: "In all their affliction He was afflicted."
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש backs up the same idea with a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The message stays the same: הקב״ה shares Israel's suffering. Only the source changes, so this is a second פסוק for one idea, not an argument.

keyTerms.meaning: in all their trouble, He is troubled

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
"In all their affliction He was afflicted."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 63:9

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק for the same answer as Step 15

steps.title: רבי זירא trembled at the sight
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells how his whole body used to shake when he saw ashes being put on the תיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: At first, whenever I saw the Rabbis putting burnt ashes on the ark, my whole body would tremble.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא shares a personal story about how strongly this practice affected him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds no new reason or law. It shows how powerful the idea from Steps 15-16 is: seeing the symbol of הקב״ה's presence covered in ashes shook him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: מֵרֵישׁ כִּי הֲוָה חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
phrases.english: At first, when I would see the Rabbis

phrases.aramaic: דְּיָהֲבִי אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה עַל גַּבֵּי תֵּיבָה —
phrases.english: placing burnt ashes on top of the ark,
my whole body would tremble.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרֵישׁ כִּי הֲוָה חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the topic of ashes on the תיבה with a personal story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sight of ashes on the תיבה is deeply moving

steps.title: Why put ashes on each person's head?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ashes are put on every person's head.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they put ashes on the head of each and every person?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next practice, ashes on each person's head. This sets up an argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the ashes went on the תיבה. Now the ashes go on each individual, and the גמרא asks what that is meant to say.

phrases.english: And why do they place ashes
on the head of each and every one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמָּה נוֹתְנִין אֵפֶר בְּרֹאשׁ כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next practice on the list
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for ashes on each person's head

steps.title: Two reasons: humility or remembering יצחק
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי בר חמא and רבי חנינא argue. One says the ashes mean we are like ashes. The other says they remind הקב״ה of the ashes of יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר חמא and רבי חנינא disagree. One says: We are considered like ashes before You. The other says: So that He will remember for us the ashes of יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different reasons for the ashes on each head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason is humility: we are nothing, like ashes. The second asks for merit: the ashes stand for יצחק, who was ready to be a sacrifice, so הקב״ה should remember his merit for us. The גמרא does not say which אמורא said which.

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Levi bar Ḥama and Rabbi Ḥanina disagree about this.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: הֲרֵי אָנוּ חֲשׁוּבִין לְפָנֶיךָ כְּאֵפֶר,
phrases.english: One said: Behold, we are considered before You like ashes,
and one said: So that He will remember for us
the ashes of Isaac.
phrases.notes: This points to יצחק at the עקידה, as if he had been offered up and turned to ash.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 with two opinions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either humility (like ashes) or a reminder of יצחק's merit

steps.title: Is there a practical difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons for the ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever lead to a different practice. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as Step 8. The גמרא wants a real case where the two opinions would act differently.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two opinions of Step 19 differ in practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons give different results

steps.title: The difference: plain earth
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether plain earth may be used instead of ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is plain earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reasons split on using ordinary dirt instead of ashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the humility reason, earth also shows we are lowly, so it works. Under the יצחק reason, only ashes recall the עקידה, so plain earth does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: there is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: Ashes on the head: humility (earth is fine too) or remembering יצחק (it must be ashes).

phrases.english: There is a difference between them regarding plain earth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ עָפָר סְתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Plain earth works under the humility reason but not under the יצחק reason

steps.title: Why go out to the cemetery?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why people go out to the cemetery on a fast day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do they go out to the cemetery?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about another fast-day practice, visiting the cemetery. This sets up a second argument between the same two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the next item on the memory list from Step 4 (קבורה, burial). The גמרא asks about it the same way: what message does it send?

phrases.english: Why do they go out to the cemetery?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה יוֹצְאִין לְבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to another fast-day practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for visiting the cemetery on a fast day

steps.title: Two reasons: we are like the dead, or the dead pray for us
steps.stepSummary: One אמורא says going to the cemetery shows we are like the dead. The other says it is so the dead will ask for mercy for us.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר חמא and רבי חנינא disagree. One says: We are considered before You like the dead. The other says: So that the dead will ask for mercy for us.
steps.whatsHappening: The same two אמוראים again give two different reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern matches the ashes argument. One reason is humility: we are like the dead. The other asks for help: the dead will pray for us.

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Levi bar Ḥama and Rabbi Ḥanina disagree about this.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: הֲרֵי אָנוּ חֲשׁוּבִין לְפָנֶיךָ כְּמֵתִים,
phrases.english: One said: Behold, we are considered before You like the dead,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּבַקְּשׁוּ עָלֵינוּ מֵתִים רַחֲמִים.
phrases.english: and one said: So that the dead will ask for mercy on our behalf.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 22 with two opinions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either humility (like the dead) or so the dead will pray for us

steps.title: What is the practical difference here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks how the two reasons differ in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a case where the two cemetery reasons would lead to different actions. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It uses the same question it asked about the ashes in Step 20.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opinions of Step 23 differ
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two cemetery reasons give different results

steps.title: The difference: graves of non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether visiting graves of non-Jews is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is graves of non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reasons split on visiting a non-Jewish cemetery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the point is 'we are like the dead,' any graves will do. If the point is that the dead should pray for us, it has to be Jewish graves.
steps.whatToRemember: Cemetery: humility (any graves are fine) or asking the dead to pray (Jewish graves only).

phrases.english: There is a difference between them regarding graves of gentiles.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ קִבְרֵי נׇכְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Non-Jewish graves work under the humility reason but not under the prayer reason

steps.title: What does the name הר המוריה mean?
steps.stepSummary: Since it is quoting arguments between these two אמוראים, the גמרא brings one more: what the name הר המוריה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'הר המוריה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the fast-day practices and asks about the name of the Temple Mount. It is grouping another argument between the same two אמוראים, and this sets up their answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side topic. The link is the people arguing, not the subject. The question is about where the name comes from.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of Mount Moriah?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הַר הַמּוֹרִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another argument between the same two אמוראים on an unrelated topic
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the name מוריה comes from

steps.title: Teaching for Israel or fear for the nations
steps.stepSummary: One says מוריה comes from הוראה, the teaching that went out to Israel. The other says it comes from מורא, the fear that went out to the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר חמא and רבי חנינא disagree. One says: The mountain from which teaching went out to Israel. The other says: The mountain from which fear went out to the nations of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The two אמוראים explain the name מוריה by linking it to two different Hebrew words that sound like it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One links מוריה to הוראה, the teaching and rulings that came from that place. The other links it to מורא, the fear that the nations felt because of it. Both make a sound-alike play on the name.
steps.whatToRemember: מוריה = הוראה (teaching to Israel) or מורא (fear for the nations).

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Levi bar Ḥama and Rabbi Ḥanina disagree about this.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: הַר שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ הוֹרָאָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: One said: The mountain from which instruction went out to Israel,
phrases.notes: He hears the word הוראה, teaching, inside the name מוריה.

phrases.english: and one said: The mountain from which went out
fear to the nations of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי לֵוִי בַּר חָמָא וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 26 with two opinions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מוריה comes from הוראה (teaching) or from מורא (fear)

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the elder gives words of rebuke
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: on a fast day, the eldest among the people speaks words of rebuke to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The eldest among them says words of rebuke in front of them.
steps.whatsHappening: After the side discussions between the two אמוראים, the גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its next line. This quote sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the order of a public fast day. After the ash is put on the ark and on people's heads, an elder stands up and speaks words that move the people toward תשובה. The גמרא now explains who this 'elder' should be.

keyTerms.meaning: Words of rebuke that 'press down' on the heart and move people to repent

phrases.english: The eldest among them says before them
words of rebuke.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַזָּקֵן שֶׁבָּהֶן אוֹמֵר לִפְנֵיהֶן דִּבְרֵי כִבּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the fast-day practices and the name מוריה (steps 4-27), returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a public fast day, the eldest of the community speaks words of rebuke to the people.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives the order of who should speak
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says: if there is an elder, the elder speaks; if not, a חכם; if not, a person of impressive appearance.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If there is an elder, the elder speaks. If not, a חכם speaks. If not, a person of impressive appearance speaks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sets out a ranking of who should give the rebuke on a fast day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only mentions the elder. The ברייתא adds backups for when no elder is present: first a חכם, then someone whose look commands respect. As written, the ranking seems to put age ahead of learning, and the next step questions exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: A person of impressive, dignified appearance

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If there is an elder, the elder speaks.
And if not, a Sage speaks,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אוֹמֵר אָדָם שֶׁל צוּרָה.
phrases.english: and if not, a person of impressive appearance speaks.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אִם יֵשׁ זָקֵן אוֹמֵר זָקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and expands the משנה's 'elder' by giving a full order of who speaks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Order of speakers: elder, then חכם, then a person of impressive appearance.

steps.title: Does an unlearned elder really come before a Sage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does the ברייתא really mean that an elder comes first even if he is not a חכם?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that the elder they are talking about comes first even though he is not a חכם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's order. It seems strange that age alone would beat Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the elder before the חכם. Read simply, that means an old man with no learning is picked over a young scholar. The גמרא finds this hard to accept, since learning should matter more than age.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces a challenge to a simple reading)

phrases.english: Is that to say that the elder they spoke of comes first,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָאו חָכָם הוּא?
phrases.english: even though he is not a Sage?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ זָקֵן דְּקָאָמְרִי אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָאו חָכָם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ranking given in the ברייתא of step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ranking of the elder above the חכם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes no sense for an unlearned elder to come before a Torah scholar.

steps.title: אביי: it means an elder who is also a Sage
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ברייתא means an elder who is also a חכם. If there is none, any חכם speaks, and if there is no חכם, a person of impressive appearance speaks.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what it means. If there is an elder who is also a חכם, he speaks. If not, a חכם speaks. If not, a person of impressive appearance speaks.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא's 'elder' as an elder who is also learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'elder' means 'elder who is also a חכם,' learning never loses to age. An older scholar comes first, then a younger scholar, and only if there is no scholar at all does a respectable-looking person speak.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; introduces a reading that explains the text differently

steps.whatToRemember: The order for the fast-day rebuke: an elder who is also a חכם, then any חכם, then a person of impressive appearance. Learning comes before age alone.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it is saying:
If there is an elder who is also a Sage,
the elder who is a Sage speaks,
and if not, a Sage speaks,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אוֹמֵר אָדָם שֶׁל צוּרָה.
phrases.english: and if not, a person of impressive appearance speaks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30 by explaining the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording ('elder' means an elder who is also a חכם)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא put an unlearned elder ahead of a חכם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first choice is an elder who is also a חכם; any חכם comes before a person chosen only for his appearance.

steps.title: The words of rebuke: תשובה, not sackcloth, brings atonement
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the elder's words: Sackcloth and fasting do not bring atonement; תשובה and good deeds do. Proof: with אנשי נינוה the פסוק speaks of their deeds, not their sackcloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our brothers, sackcloth and fasting do not bring atonement; תשובה and good deeds do. We see this with the people of נינוה. The פסוק does not say 'God saw their sackcloth and their fasting.' It says: 'God saw their deeds, that they turned from their evil way.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the text of the משנה telling us what the elder actually says to the people on the fast day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The message is that the outside signs of a fast are only tools. Real change comes from fixing one's actions. The proof is from the wording of יונה: the פסוק could have mentioned the sackcloth and fasting, but it mentions only that they turned from their evil ways.

keyTerms.meaning: Sackcloth, rough cloth worn in mourning or fasting
The people of the city of נינוה, from the book of יונה

steps.whatToRemember: The heart of a fast day is תשובה and good deeds. The sackcloth and fasting are only there to help bring people to that.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the central message of every public fast: the outside actions only help if they lead to real change in how we act.

phrases.english: Our brothers, it is not sackcloth and fasting that cause atonement,
rather, repentance and good deeds cause it.
For so we find with the people of Nineveh,
that it is not said about them:
"And God saw their sackcloth and their fasting,"
rather: "And God saw their deeds,"
"that they had turned from their evil way."
phrases.notes: יונה 3:10

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחֵינוּ לֹא שַׂק וְתַעֲנִית גּוֹרְמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's text, giving the actual words the elder of step 28 says.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Atonement comes from תשובה and good deeds, not from sackcloth and fasting alone; proven from the wording about אנשי נינוה.

steps.title: What did נינוה do when covering animals in sackcloth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק 'Let man and beast be covered with sackcloth' and asks what the people of נינוה actually did.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Let them be covered with sackcloth, man and beast.' What did they do?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the משנה mentioned אנשי נינוה, the גמרא now looks more closely at what they did. It quotes a פסוק and asks what it means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting sackcloth on animals seems odd, since animals do not sin or repent. The גמרא wants to know what real action stood behind this, and how it helped their prayer.

phrases.english: "And let them be covered with sackcloth, man and beast":
phrases.notes: יונה 3:8

phrases.english: What did they do?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיִתְכַּסּוּ שַׂקִּים הָאָדָם וְהַבְּהֵמָה מַאי הֲווֹ עָבְדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the mention of אנשי נינוה from step 32 and opens a side discussion about their תשובה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical action lay behind covering the animals with sackcloth.

steps.title: They separated mother animals from their young
steps.stepSummary: The people of נינוה tied up the mother animals in one place and their young in another. Then they told ה׳: if You do not have mercy on us, we will not have mercy on these animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: They tied up the animals separately and the young ones separately. They said to Him: Master of the world! If You do not have mercy on us, we will not have mercy on these.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the people of נינוה separated the animals from their babies so they would cry out, and used this to plead with ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hungry babies and their mothers cried to each other. The people tied their own fate to the animals: the animals did nothing wrong, so ה׳ should show mercy to the people for the animals' sake. This was a strong, almost forceful way of asking for mercy.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the world (a way of addressing ה׳)

phrases.english: They tied up the animals separately,
phrases.notes: He means the mother animals.

phrases.english: and the young separately.
They said before Him: Master of the Universe!
If You do not have mercy on us,
we will not have mercy on these.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָסְרוּ הַבְּהֵמוֹת לְחוּד וְאֶת הַוְּולָדוֹת לְחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They separated mother animals from their young and told ה׳ they would not pity the animals unless He pitied them.

steps.title: What did נינוה cry out 'with strength'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'And let them call out to God with strength' and asks what they said.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And let them call out to God with strength.' What did they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at another phrase in the same פסוק and asks what words the people of נינוה used that could be called crying out 'with strength.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'with strength' suggests more than a normal prayer. The גמרא wants to know what bold argument they made.

phrases.english: "And let them cry mightily to God":
phrases.notes: יונה 3:8, the same פסוק as before.

phrases.english: What did they say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיִקְרְאוּ אֶל אֱלֹהִים בְּחׇזְקָה מַאי אֲמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the same פסוק about אנשי נינוה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What words of prayer counted as crying out 'with strength.'

steps.title: Their bold plea: who should give in to whom?
steps.stepSummary: They said to ה׳: between one who is humble and one who is not, between a צדיק and a רשע, who should give way to whom?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to Him: Master of the world! Between someone humble and someone who is not, between a צדיק and a רשע, who should give in to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: their 'strong' prayer was a bold argument that the greater one should give way to the lesser one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their point is that in a fight, the humble and righteous one is expected to give in and forgive. ה׳ is the perfectly righteous one and they are the sinners, so He should forgive them. That daring argument is what the פסוק calls crying out 'with strength.'

keyTerms.meaning: Humble, one who takes insult quietly
A righteous person and a wicked person

steps.whatToRemember: אנשי נינוה prayed boldly: they used the animals to arouse mercy, and they argued that the righteous one, ה׳, should yield and forgive the wicked.

phrases.english: They said before Him: Master of the Universe!
One who is humble and one who is not humble,
a righteous one and a wicked one:
who yields before whom?
phrases.notes: They leave the answer unsaid: the righteous one gives in, so ה׳ should forgive them.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָלוּב וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ עָלוּב צַדִּיק וְרָשָׁע מִי נִדְחֶה מִפְּנֵי מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argued that the humble and righteous one, ה׳, should give way and forgive the wicked.

steps.title: What was the 'violence in their hands' in נינוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another phrase from the נינוה פסוק and asks what 'the violence that is in their hands' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Let every man turn from his evil way and from the violence that is in their hands.' What does 'the violence that is in their hands' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going through the פסוקים about נינוה, one phrase at a time. Now it asks about 'the violence in their hands', setting up שמואל's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the earlier questions about the sackcloth and the crying out. The גמרא wants to know exactly what the people of נינוה did to fix the stealing in their hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Violence or robbery; taking what belongs to someone else

phrases.english: "And let them turn, every man from his evil way,
phrases.notes: יונה 3:8

phrases.english: and from the violence that is in their hands."
What is "and from the violence that is in their hands"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וּמִן הֶחָמָס אֲשֶׁר בְּכַפֵּיהֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of questions on the נינוה פסוקים (steps 33 and 35).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did the people of נינוה actually do to turn away from 'the violence in their hands'?

steps.title: They tore down whole buildings to return one stolen beam
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that even someone who built a stolen beam into a building would tear down the whole building to give the beam back.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Even if a person stole a beam and built it into a big building, he would tear down the whole building and give the beam back to its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question: the people of נינוה returned stolen things completely, no matter how much it cost them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that their תשובה was not just words or sackcloth. They got rid of every trace of the stealing, even when it meant destroying a whole building to free one beam. This goes beyond what the regular הלכה demands from a thief, which shows how serious their תשובה was.

keyTerms.meaning: A beam (a large piece of wood used in building)

steps.whatToRemember: The תשובה of נינוה was real action: they gave back what they stole, even at a huge cost.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Even if one stole a beam
and built it into a building,
he tears down the entire building, all of it,
and returns the beam to its owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֲפִילּוּ גָּזַל מָרִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The people of נינוה returned stolen property completely, even tearing down a whole building to return one stolen beam.

steps.title: Confessing without leaving the sin is like immersing while holding a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה compares someone who confesses a sin but keeps doing it to a person who immerses in a מקוה while still holding a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: A person who has a sin, confesses it, but does not stop doing it, what is he like? He is like someone holding a dead שרץ in his hand. Even if he dips in all the water in the world, the טבילה does not help. Once he throws it away and dips in a מקוה of forty סאה, the טבילה works right away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה gives a parable that continues the theme of real תשובה: saying sorry is useless if you are still holding on to the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שרץ is what makes the person טמא, so as long as he holds it, no amount of water helps. In the same way, the sin is what needs fixing, so confession without stopping the sin does nothing. Once the source is let go, even a small, regular amount (a normal מקוה) works immediately.

keyTerms.meaning: Confesses (says out loud what he did wrong)
Turns back from it; stops doing the sin
A creeping creature; when dead, touching it makes a person טמא
Immersion in a מקוה to become טהור
Forty סאה, the minimum amount of water for a kosher מקוה

steps.confusionAlert: The point is not that the water is weak. A small, normal מקוה works perfectly, but only after he lets go of the שרץ. The problem is what he is still holding.
steps.whatToRemember: Confession only works together with leaving the sin, just like טבילה only works after you let go of the שרץ.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
A person who has a sin in his hand,
and he confesses but does not turn back from it,
to what is he comparable?
To a person who holds a dead creeping creature in his hand,
phrases.notes: Touching a dead שרץ makes a person טמא, so he stays טמא as long as he holds it.

phrases.english: that even if he immerses in all the waters in the world,
his immersion does not work for him.
If he threw it from his hand,
once he immersed in forty se'ah,
phrases.notes: Forty סאה is just the normal minimum size of a מקוה, nothing special.

phrases.english: immediately his immersion works for him,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּיָדוֹ עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new teaching on the same theme: like נינוה, real תשובה means letting go of the sin itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Confession without abandoning the sin is useless, like immersing while holding a שרץ; once the sin is abandoned, תשובה works right away.

steps.title: Two פסוקים prove that confession must come with leaving the sin
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה supports his parable with a פסוק from משלי (confess AND leave) and a פסוק from איכה (lift the heart, not just the hands).
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'One who confesses and leaves them will receive mercy.' And it also says: 'Let us lift up our heart with our hands to God in heaven.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה brings פסוקים to prove his point from step 39.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says mercy comes to one who confesses AND leaves the sin, not just confesses. The second פסוק says lifting the hands in prayer is not enough; the heart must be lifted too, meaning a real inner change.

keyTerms.meaning: And it says (introduces a second פסוק as more proof)

phrases.english: As it is said: "But whoever confesses and leaves them will receive mercy."
phrases.notes: משלי 28:13

phrases.english: And it says:
"Let us lift up our heart with our hands
to God in heaven."
phrases.notes: איכה 3:41

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּמוֹדֶה וְעֹזֵב יְרֻחָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוקים behind רב אדא בר אהבה's parable.
steps.raayaObject: Confession alone does not bring atonement; one must also abandon the sin.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 28:13 ('confesses and leaves') and איכה 3:41 ('lift our heart with our hands').

steps.title: Only someone 'accustomed' leads the prayers on a fast day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about sending an elder before the תיבה, and quotes a ברייתא: even if an elder and scholar is present, only a person who is 'רגיל' leads.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: They stood for prayer and sent an elder before the ark. The Rabbis taught: They stood for prayer; even if there is an elder and a scholar there, they only send before the ark a person who is accustomed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה: who should be the שליח ציבור on a fast day. It quotes a ברייתא that sets a requirement of being 'רגיל', and the next step will explain what that means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being old and learned is not enough. The ברייתא says the leader must be 'רגיל', and the following lines describe what kind of person counts as 'רגיל'.

keyTerms.meaning: The ark, the place where the שליח ציבור stands to lead
They send down (appoint someone to lead the prayers)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'רגיל' just means someone who leads often. The ברייתא goes on to describe a specific kind of person, so wait for the next lines.

phrases.english: They stood for prayer,
they send down before the ark an elder, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
They stood for prayer,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם זָקֵן וְחָכָם
phrases.english: even though there is an elder and a scholar there,
they do not send down before the ark
anyone except a person who is accustomed.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמְדוּ בִּתְפִלָּה, מוֹרִידִין לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה זָקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the נינוה discussion and returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a fast day, even when an elder and scholar is present, only a person who is 'רגיל' is sent to lead the prayers.

steps.title: רבי יהודה describes the right prayer leader: needy and hardworking
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה begins describing the ideal leader: he has a family to feed and no money, he works hard in the field, and his house is empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: One who has a family to support and has nothing, who toils in the field, and whose house is empty,
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה starts to describe what kind of person should lead the prayers on a fast day. His list continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every detail describes someone who truly needs the rain: hungry mouths to feed, a field that depends on rain, and nothing in the house. Such a person will pray from the heart.

keyTerms.meaning: Burdened with a family (children to support)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who has a family to support and has nothing,
and he has toil in the field,
and his house is empty,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מְטוּפָּל וְאֵין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what kind of person fits the ברייתא's requirement of a 'רגיל' leader.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast-day leader should be someone truly in need: with a family, no money, working in the field, and an empty house (list continues).

steps.title: רבי יהודה finishes listing the leader's qualities
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds more qualities to his picture of the ideal leader: a clean past, humility, being liked by people, a sweet voice, and expert knowledge of all of תנ"ך, מדרש, הלכות, אגדות and the ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And his younger years were fitting, and he is humble and accepted by the people. He knows how to sing and his voice is pleasant. He is expert in reading the תורה, the נביאים and the כתובים, and in learning מדרש, הלכות and אגדות, and he is expert in all of the ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing the same list from רבי יהודה that started in the last step. Here he adds character traits, voice, and learning to the earlier traits of being poor and hard-working.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 42 gave the leader's life situation: a family to feed, no money, and an empty house, so he prays from the heart. This step adds three new kinds of qualities: good character (a clean past, humble, liked by people), a good voice, and broad knowledge. The point is that the leader must be both sincere and fully skilled.

keyTerms.meaning: His younger years were fitting and proper
Accepted by and pleasing to the people
Melody, knowing how to sing pleasantly
The main areas of תורה שבעל פה: explaining the פסוקים, laws, and stories and lessons

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion. It is the same sentence of רבי יהודה from step 42 continuing, so all these traits belong to one long description.

phrases.english: And his younger years were fitting,
phrases.notes: פרקו literally means 'his stage of life'. Here it points to his younger years.

phrases.english: and he is humble,
and accepted by the people,
and he knows how to sing, and his voice is pleasant,
and he is expert in reading the Torah
and the Prophets and the Writings,
and in learning midrash,
halachot and aggadot,
and he is expert in all of the blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפִרְקוֹ נָאֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהודה's description of the ideal leader that began in step 42.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ideal leader on a תענית must also have a clean past, be humble and liked, have a pleasant voice, and be expert in תנ"ך, מדרש, הלכות, אגדות and all the ברכות.

steps.title: The Sages look at רב יצחק בר אמי
steps.stepSummary: When the full list was said, the Sages all turned to look at רב יצחק בר אמי, showing that he was a person with all these qualities.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages turned their eyes toward רב יצחק בר אמי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. As soon as the list was finished, all the Sages looked at רב יצחק בר אמי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list sounds almost impossible to fulfill, so the story shows that such a person really existed. Looking at him was a quiet way of saying 'this describes you.' It also gives honor to רב יצחק בר אמי.

keyTerms.meaning: They put their eyes on, they all looked at

steps.whatToRemember: The leader on a תענית must be sincere (poor and hard-working), of good character, pleasant-voiced, and very learned. The Sages saw all of this in רב יצחק בר אמי.

phrases.english: And the Sages turned their eyes
toward Rav Yitzchak bar Ami.

steps.triggerLanguage: וִיהַבוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן עֵינַיְיהוּ בְּרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A short story that closes רבי יהודה's list by pointing to a real person who fit it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Sages saw רב יצחק בר אמי as someone who had every quality on the list.
